messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike detected across eu-west-1 GPU pool. Metrics: p95=210ms (SLO 150ms), p99=1.9s (SLO 500ms). Error type: streaming stalls / paging. Autotrigger: paging_eviction_rate increased by 4x.
Sam: seeing the same in dashboards. Streaming requests are timing out in the tail — lots of OPEN_STREAM stalls.
Maria: Customer reports incoming: two mid-market customers showing elevated errors. Ticket IDs: #C-8442, #C-8443. Potential revenue-sensitive.
Lee: any rolling kernel/compile pushes in the last 6h? I just got a deploy notification earlier for trt8 kernels on eu-west GPU pool.
Jordan: yes, we rolled trt8 + flashattn 2.1 builds at ~06:30UTC to 50% canary. Flags: --compiler-opts="-O2 -fast-math -fno-rtti" (internal).
Sam: that matches timeline. Paging spike started ~06:42UTC. Can we confirm canary traffic % and whether canary expanded?
Ops-bot: Canary expansion log: canary -> 50% at 06:30, no automated expand. No rollback triggered.
Maria: quick impact check — what models/tenants hit the p99? Is it single-tenant Dedicated or hosted?
Sam: mostly hosted inference, model family rdx-13b-quant and a few larger 30b variants. Request shape: many streaming chat sessions with long context (~8k tokens).
Lee: long contexts + trt8 flashattn combo is suspicious. Could be a kernel micro-regression causing increased memory pressure and page faults during KV cache growth.
Jordan: I can grab kernel logs from the canary nodes. Running: `journalctl -u inference-runtime --since "06:20" | grep -i page`
Sam: also start sampling a few live traces for blocked syscalls, `strace -f -p <pid>` on a suspect instance (off-hours low impact). Keep traces to 10s windows.
Maria: I'm pinging support to notify customers and create status page draft. Short blurb: "We are investigating increased latency in eu-west-1 affecting streaming sessions; mitigation steps underway."
Ops-bot: Telemetry snapshot saved to /tmp/incident-3897654321.tar.gz (metrics + traces + kernel logs).
Lee: log excerpt: `mm: page fault on GPU pinned memory: eviction triggered, compilepath fallback engaged` and `flashattn: kernel_launch_time jitter +42%` — looks like new kernel path occasionally falls back to slow codepath under load.
Jordan: suggestion: set routing policy to avoid canary instances and force traffic to the previous kernel image. We can also temporarily reduce long-context batch size to lower KV cache pressure.
Sam: Agreed. Plan: 1) Reroute traffic off canary nodes. 2) Toggle `runtime:enable_prefix_cache=true` on heavy tenants. 3) If still bad, roll back trt8 kernel image for eu-west pool.
Lee: I'll run the reroute now: `rctl route update --pool eu-west-1 --exclude-image=trt8-flashattn-2026-03-12`
Jordan: executing. Patch applied. Monitoring for 2 minutes.
Sam: watch p95/p99 on streaming-latency.v2 and paging_eviction_rate.
Maria: I pushed the customer status update draft to #status-drafts, ready for approval.
Ops-bot: Route update succeeded. Active sessions draining from canary nodes.
Sam: early signals: p95 dropped to 160ms, p99 trending down to 800ms but still above SLO. Paging_eviction_rate falling.
Lee: good. I'll also flip compiler flag `-fast-math` off on the canary image and run a small A/B to see if numeric changes reduce fallback. Command: `rbuild tag trt8-flashattn-2026-03-12-no-fastmath` then canary.
Jordan: can we also enable aggressive prefix cache for the affected models? `config set model rdx-13b-quant prefix_cache=aggressive` Should cut repeated decode work.
Sam: done for two biggest tenants. Early reduction in tokens processed per request observed (~18% less).
Maria: customers acknowledged update and asked for ETA. I told them we expect stabilization in <2 hours and will follow up in 30m.
Lee: p99 now at 420ms. That’s within SLO for most requests. Streaming stalls frequency reduced significantly.
Jordan: Recommend delaying kernel merge of trt8 flashattn until we validate on extended load tests and build a fallback safe-mode.
Sam: agree. Next actions: - Hold rollout. - Run extended soak on canary with long-context loads. - Prepare rollback playbook notes. - Postmortem owner assign.
Maria: I'll set the incident severity to P2 and assign customer comms owner (Nora). Nora: can you coordinate postmortem and customer follow-up?
Nora: on it. I'll collect logs, timelines, and confirm which customers saw errors. Starting a repo: `incidents/3897654321` and will drop artifacts there.
Ops-bot: Incident severity set to P2 by Maria. Handoff reminder: night-oncall will pick at 00:00UTC.
Sam: handing off to night oncall — leave playbook: if p99 > 600ms re-open and escalate to eng-runtime pager. Keep routing off trt8 until soak passes.
Lee: added notes about the kernel micro-regression: possible causes = kernel scheduling jitter + flashattn kernel path memory assumptions.
Jordan: I'll spin a targeted perf test for rdx-13b-quant with 8k contexts to reproduce in staging and test patched kernels.
Maria: thanks everyone. I'll update status page once we confirm full recovery. :thumbsup:
Nora: collecting artifacts now, will draft timeline and owner list for postmortem. :eyes:
